work.title: Redwood front-door ingestion and UX acceptance path

intent.productGoal: Enable a professional user to create a new engagement and bring unfamiliar evidence through the product UI into a governed canonical engagement.
intent.capability: New engagement, ZIP/individual source intake, source inventory/recognition/preview, mapping, G1 sufficiency, immutable run creation, and Reconcile handoff.
architecturalIntent: Build on the existing Redwood Workbench rather than a parallel application.
Drive evidence enters only through user-facing intake; hidden truth is excluded from normal ingestion.
invariants: Original source bytes and hashes remain preserved.
No silent source coercion or back-door test injection.
Visible active engagement values derive from uploaded evidence.
acceptanceEvidence: Challenge A front-door journey trace and hidden post-run comparison.
Automated engine and UI journey tests.

observedBehaviour: Challenge A ZIP was materialized from Drive file ID 1_51XjIUG52kvYxLvTAKaMsx0SjTExjSW with SHA-256 9d48c8b4a585f75bf912a72c3f9789fd0ef8bd4db6259904b9e561071c2acf17.
ZIP intake inventories 11 entries and excludes Validation_Truth from canonical source candidates.
Raw source populations contain 480 claims, 635 payments, 209 A/R rows, and 12 GL rows.

evidence.reference: Challenge A ZIP front-door API trace
evidence.result: Created run 1b248405-eec1-42dd-8660-874946a0b97e from original ZIP bytes without reading Validation_Truth.
ZIP inventory, source preview, mapping and G1 display implemented.

divergences.expected: Run Redwood is enabled only after an explicit front-door G1 review, then reaches Reconcile through the visible user journey.
divergences.observed: Current intake constructs a run immediately after source submission; a separate G1 approval/run transition and browser-level journey evidence remain incomplete.
